text:
Lake Wind Advisory first: if you’re taking a boat out, today is a rougher proposition than the cloudy, quiet start suggests. South winds will build to 15 to 25 knots, with waves around 1 to 3 feet, while Burlington stays mostly dry through the afternoon and tops out near 77. The models disagree on how quickly rain arrives, but the forecasters’ call is clear enough: showers and thunderstorms move in after sunset, with the steadiest, potentially heavy rain tonight and around a half to three-quarters of an inch possible. Winds could gust to 30 mph, and lake waves may build as high as 3 to 5 feet.

Thursday stays unsettled, with a high near 79 and a 70% chance of showers and thunderstorms, mainly before late afternoon. Winds and waves should ease, but I’d keep outdoor plans flexible. Enjoy the dry window today, stay off the broad lake by late afternoon, and have rain gear ready before dinner.
